1. (Currently Amended) An assembly comprising a test tube with a light-activated microtransponder (MTP) affixed thereto, wherein the MTP is responsive to light activation for identification and tracking of the test tube.

2. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded in the test tube and is activated by light exposure to transmit identification data.

3. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded underneath the bottom of the test tube, oriented for reading downwards, and wherein the MTP comprises a light-activated component distinct from passive RFID technology.

4. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the test tube is a biorepository test tube designed for long-term storage of biological samples, and wherein the MTP is a light-activated microtransponder rather than a passive RFID tag.

5. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded in polypropylene or acetal polymer, and wherein the MTP is light-activated to provide real-time identification and tracking capabilities.

6. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 1, wherein the MTP is embedded near the center bottom of the test tube, and wherein the test tube comprises the container for the MTP.

13. (Currently Amended) A system for storing samples comprising the assembly of claim 1, and one or more of the following: a rack for biorepository test tubes; an automated robot for moving racks or biorepository test tubes; and an automated sampling device adapted to sample said racks or biorepository test tubes, wherein the system utilizes light-activated microtransponders for sample identification and tracking.

14. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 13 adapted for low temperature operation, such that the racks and test tubes are handled at -20°C or less, and wherein the light-activated microtransponders remain functional at such temperatures.

15. (Currently Amended) A method of forming a test tube assembly of claim 1, comprising: heating a light-activated microtransponder to above the melting point of plastic; and melting a portion of the plastic with the heated MTP to embed the light-activated microtransponder within the plastic material.

16. (Currently Amended) A method of reading an embedded light-activated microtransponder in a test tube assembly of claim 1, comprising: providing an embedded light-activated MTP; exposing the MTP to light activation; and reading identification data transmitted by the MTP in response to light activation.

17. (Currently Amended) The method of reading of claim 16, wherein the embedding material is frost coated to protect the light-activated MTP.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 16, wherein the reader comprises a vial receptacle and wherein the vial receptacle and the embedded light-activated MTP are maintained at a temperature of -20°C or less.

19. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 4, wherein the MTP is embedded in polypropylene or acetal polymer, and wherein the MTP is a light-activated microtransponder.

20. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 19, wherein the MTP is embedded near the center bottom of the test tube.

21. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 19, wherein the MTP is embedded underneath the bottom of the test tube, oriented for reading downwards.

22. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 4, wherein the MTP is embedded near the center bottom of the test tube, and wherein the MTP is a light-activated microtransponder distinct from passive RFID technology.

23. (Currently Amended) The assembly of claim 4, wherein the MTP is embedded underneath the bottom of the test tube, oriented for reading downwards, and wherein the MTP comprises a light-activated component.
